papers.title_en: AgentEvolver: System-Wide Self-Evolution Through Task Execution
papers.authors: Wentao Zhang, Fuchao Yang, Yilei Zhao, Xinrun Wang, Bo An
papers.evidence: 在保持基础模型不变的前提下实现系统级自我演化
papers.tldr: 智能体完成任务并不意味着其工作方式得到改进，把任务经验转化为可复用能力需要将改动组件与其评估和后续使用相连接。作者提出AgentEvolver，在保持基础模型固定的前提下，让八类实体通过统一的版本化生命周期被修订，并由共享运行时协调。在SWE-bench Pro Public与六个应用案例上的评估显示能力变化，为区分系统级自我演化与更强基座模型提供了参照。
papers.abstract_en: An agent can complete a task without improving how it works. Turning task experience into reusable capability requires connecting the changed component to its evaluation and subsequent use. We present AgentEvolver, a system for developing capabilities during task execution while keeping the foundation model fixed. Eight entity families expose reusable operations, methods, agents, control flow, interfaces, and supporting state to revision through a common versioned lifecycle. A shared Runtime coordinates ongoing work, while persistent planning and recoverable context preserve task direction and supporting evidence. We evaluate task outcomes on SWE-bench Pro Public and examine capability changes in six application cases. The team reports an 82.08\% resolution rate with evolution, exceeding its reported baseline without evolution. The cases show retained capabilities entering later website, game, and research work, while also documenting incomplete objectives and an unsuccessful strategy. These findings distinguish improvement in a reusable component from success on the final task. AgentEvolver provides a concrete basis for studying capability accumulation through execution; independent-task transfer and total development cost remain open questions.

papers.title_en: PRAXIS: Learning Dynamics of Self-Improving Models with Symbolic Archives
papers.evidence: 带符号档案的自改进模型学习动力学的理论分析
papers.tldr: 自改进学习系统会自适应调整数据选择、优化与辅助符号组件，从而产生偏离标准学习假设的非平稳目标。作者提出 PRAXIS 协同演化框架，将生成器、学习器与符号档案建模为相互作用的动力学过程，并给出 KL 约束生成器更新与档案权重变化对单步目标漂移的界。理论结果还给出随机梯度下降的平均平稳性保证，其退化程度由累积目标漂移控制。该工作为理解自改进系统的训练稳定性提供理论工具。
papers.abstract_en: Self-improving learning systems adapt data selection, optimization, and auxiliary symbolic components, inducing nonstationary objectives outside standard learning assumptions. We introduce \textsc{PRAXIS}, a co-evolutionary framework that models generators, learners, and symbolic archives as interacting dynamical processes. We prove that KL-constrained generator updates and controlled archive-weight movement bound one-step objective drift, that archive updates suppress a program relative to any fixed comparator with a persistent cumulative utility advantage under sub-Gaussian noise, and that stochastic gradient descent achieves an average-stationarity guarantee whose degradation is governed by cumulative objective drift. Experiments across visual robustness, relational graph reasoning, and algorithmic graph reasoning exhibit generator stabilization, decreasing learner loss, and archive concentration consistent with these theoretical mechanisms.

papers.title_en: ReSI: Recursive Safety Improvement toward Resistant and Resilient AI
papers.authors: Jingnan Zheng, Dongcheng Zhang, Yi Zhang, Ming Zhang, Qiaosheng Zhang, Youbang Sun, An Zhang, Xiangnan He, Tat-Seng Chua, Xia Hu, Bowen Zhou, Chaochao Lu, Xiang Wang
papers.evidence: 将递归自我改进应用于AI系统安全对齐
papers.tldr: 该文指出递归自我改进正从理论走向实践，模型频繁更新使安全对齐需持续适应新检查点。作者提出ReSI递归安全改进框架，让安全对齐也通过自我迭代推进，兼顾对已知威胁的抵抗与对未知风险的韧性。研究为自改进系统的安全对齐提供了可迭代的机制，凸显RSI与安全协同的潜力。
papers.abstract_en: Recursive self-improvement, the participation of AI systems in improving their own capabilities, is beginning to move from theoretical prospect to practice, posing both challenges and opportunities for safety alignment. Models evolve through frequent updates, and their safety alignment requires continual adaptation to each new checkpoint. Meanwhile, with evolving red-teaming methods exposing new vulnerabilities, safety improvement for each checkpoint needs to mitigate exposed vulnerabilities and generalize to risks not yet revealed. Following R$^2$AI, we term these goals resistance to known threats and resilience to unforeseen risks. Recursive self-improvement, in turn, inspires an approach to both goals: safety alignment could likewise advance through successive rounds of evaluation and update. We therefore introduce ReSI, a recursive safety improvement framework that implements this approach through automated research. In each round, ReSI applies diverse red-teaming methods to identify vulnerabilities in the current target model, develops training recipes, and promotes the update with the largest safety gain among those passing a Pareto gate on capability retention as the next target model. Across four dense and mixture-of-experts models, ReSI matches or exceeds evaluated frontier models on in-distribution and out-of-distribution safety benchmarks, and outperforms alignment baselines on nearly all safety evaluations while largely preserving general capabilities. In particular, ReSI reduces the mean X-Teaming attack success rate across the four models from 86.01% to 31.45%, well below GPT-5.6-Luna's leading frontier result of 56.69%, indicating stronger resilience to attacks unseen during training. These findings support recursive safety improvement as a practical path toward resistant and resilient AI.

papers.title_en: Language Models as AI Research World Models
papers.authors: Zijun Wang, Zewen Liu, Minhua Lin, Zhaotian Weng, Zhan Shi, Bing He, Yisi Sang, Dakuo Wang, Benoit Dumoulin, Wei Jin, Yuyin Zhou, Cihang Xie, Hanqing Lu
papers.evidence: 用语言模型作为世界模型预测实验以支撑AI研究自我改进
papers.tldr: 该文指出AI研究智能体虽能自动提出、实现并评估实验，但提出速度远超实际执行能力。作者研究语言模型作为研究世界模型，预测候选干预在不同研究环境中的结果，并基于2600余条实验记录与17万余H100 GPU时数据训练评估。结果显示真实实验经验能提升预测能力，为有限预算下持续自我改进提供关键支撑。
papers.abstract_en: AI research agents automate the cycle of proposing, implementing, and evaluating experiments, opening a path toward recursive self-improvement. Yet their ability to propose experiments outpaces their capacity to execute them in real environments, making outcome prediction a key capability for sustained self-improvement under limited experimental budgets. We investigate language models as Research World Models (RWMs), which predict the outcomes of candidate interventions across research environments. Our evaluation draws on over 2,600 experimental records from nine research environments spanning pretraining, post-training, and inference, representing more than 171,000 H100 GPU-hours of experimentation. Research knowledge acquired from real experimental experience improves RWM predictions of unseen interventions within the same environment (Spearman +0.27), and can be reused across environments. For example, using only pretraining experience from OLMo3, Marin, and Nanochat, an RWM reduces selection regret in the Qwen3 environment by 78% compared with zero-experience setting. These benefits extend to multi-round Autoresearch under a fixed selection budget: RWMs with in-env and cross-env research knowledge increase the best gain achieved by 15.8% and 11.6%, respectively. Ablations across 13 language models used as RWMs show that adding research knowledge can improve intervention ranking more than changing models or increasing reasoning effort alone. These findings support language models as RWMs and motivate accumulating experimental data for future RWM training.

papers.title_en: Agentic Data Engineering for LLMs: System Design and a Controlled Empirical Study
papers.authors: Ruomeng Ding, Qianli Shen, Zhaoyang Han, Meixin Chen, Daoyuan Chen, Yaliang Li
papers.evidence: 智能体用实验反馈自动化LLM数据工程研究
papers.tldr: 该文指出LLM数据工程需迭代实验来确定数据选择、奖励与课程如何影响学习，是AI4AI的理想场景。作者提出Agentic数据工程框架，让智能体依据累积实验反馈推进、修改或组合研究方向，并用环内分数筛选策略。在数学与代码数据选择等四类任务上，所得策略在留出基准上提升了目标模型表现，展示了智能体自动化研究流程的潜力。
papers.abstract_en: LLM data engineering requires iterative experimentation to determine how data selection, rewards, and curricula affect model learning, making it a natural setting for AI-for-AI (AI4AI) research. Can agents use experimental feedback to progressively improve strategies, and do the resulting strategies improve target-model performance on held-out data? We study how agents use experimental feedback to develop data-engineering strategies under fixed training and evaluation protocols. Our Agentic Data Engineering (ADE) framework lets agents pursue, revise, or combine research directions using cumulative findings. Strategies are selected by in-loop scores and evaluated on held-out benchmarks. Across four tasks-math and code data selection, math reward design, and math curriculum learning-selected strategies achieve absolute gains over generic baselines of up to 13.34% on AIME25 Pass@32 and 5.85% averaged across four held-out benchmarks under fixed training conditions. In-loop scores improve over successive experiments, while held-out trajectories show that later in-loop gains do not always improve generalization. Comparisons of research organization and feedback access favor combining evidence analysis with cumulative findings. Research trajectories show how earlier findings inform strategy revisions and combinations across research directions.

papers.title_en: SpecForge: Recursive Self-Improvement for Coding Agents via Behavioral Specifications
papers.authors: Yutong Cheng, Haifeng Chen, Peng Gao, Wei Cheng
papers.evidence: 通过精化行为规约的递归自我改进闭环
papers.tldr: 基于冻结语言模型的编码智能体无法更新权重，只能依靠外部上下文提升表现，但上下文如何递归精化仍具挑战。论文以行为规约作为可演化的自然语言代码文档，构建自改进闭环：智能体依当前规约生成代码，用执行验证的测试评估，再根据失败反馈精化规约以指导后续生成。实验表明规约的递归精化能逐步加深对代码库的理解并提升生成正确率，说明不改权重也能实现智能体的递归自我改进。
papers.abstract_en: Coding agents based on frozen language models can improve their performance by refining the external context they rely on, without updating model weights. We study recursive self-improvement through behavioral specifications: natural-language code documentation that describes the behavior of program entities and guides agents in generating correct code. We formulate a self-improvement loop in which an agent generates code from its current specifications, evaluates it with execution-verified tests, and refines the specifications based on observed failures. The improved specifications then guide subsequent generation, progressively improving the agent's understanding of the codebase. However, recursive refinement is challenging because program entities are interdependent. Improving the specification of one entity can inadvertently degrade the correctness of others, a phenomenon we call output coupling. This creates a whack-a-mole effect in which local improvements cause regressions elsewhere, preventing consistent progress. We introduce SpecForge, a multi-frontier tree search framework that addresses this challenge with three mechanisms: (i) Pareto-guided state selection preserves complementary specification states and prevents premature commitment; (ii) dependency-constrained entity selection prioritizes callee-before-caller refinement; and (iii) error-diversified expansion explores multiple refinements using different subsets of test failures. On DevEval+, SpecForge achieves the best performance across five backbone models, including a 94.9% solve rate with Claude-4.5-Sonnet and a 5.7-percentage-point average improvement over the strongest baseline. The improved specifications also make the agent better at tasks outside the loop: they transfer to cross-language translation and to new-feature implementation, where they outperform the benchmark-provided requirement documents.

papers.authors: Wenqian Ye, Ziwei Guan, Zi Yang, Shivani Modi, Cici Cong Wu, Yunlong He, Yuxin Chen, Zhengyu Zhang, Liang Luo, Venkatesh Ranganathan, Jianhui Sun, Yantao Yao, Wenlin Chen, Buyun Zhang, Ellie Dingqiao Wen, Henry Kautz, Aidong Zhang
papers.evidence: 通过联合进化智能体与专用模型，将递归自我改进扩展到领域专用模型。
papers.tldr: 领域专用基础模型虽具专业知识，却依赖人工设计改进，难以扩展递归自我改进。HACE提出异构智能体协同进化框架，通过相互学习联合进化专用模型与LLM智能体：专用模型接受监督学习，智能体则采用在策略强化自训练，并以验证过的性能增益为引导。该工作把递归自我改进扩展到专用模型，为自主提升领域能力提供了新思路。
papers.abstract_en: Recent advances in self-improving LLM agents have demonstrated the potential of AI systems that drive their own intelligence. However, many domain-specific applications rely on specialized foundation models that possess strong domain expertise but remain dependent on human-designed improvements. Extending recursive self-improvement to these models presents a key challenge: as a specialist improves, the strategies used to advance it must also adapt. To address this challenge, we propose Heterogeneous Agentic CoEvolution (HACE), a framework that jointly evolves specialized foundation models and LLM agents through reciprocal learning. HACE improves the specialist through supervised learning while training the agent with on-policy reinforced self-training, guided by verified performance gains on the current specialist. The agent's exploration, in turn, informs subsequent specialist training, enabling both models to adapt to each other's progress. To sustain this reciprocal learning, HACE further employs evolutionary search to optimize their interaction harness, adapting how the models exchange information and select training experiences as their capabilities evolve. We evaluate HACE across three challenging domains: recommendation systems, protein function prediction in biology, and crystal stability prediction in material discovery. We show that HACE outperforms the evaluated self-improving methods on the primary task metrics across all three domains. These results shed light on heterogeneous coevolution as a universal approach to improving specialized foundation models through reciprocal interaction with a learning agent.

papers.authors: Brian B. Moser, Stanislav Frolov, Tobias C. Nauen, Federico Raue, Andreas Dengel
papers.evidence: 形式化分析自动门控能否可靠区分真正的语义自我改进与虚假更新。
papers.tldr: 随着LLM智能体能够改写代码、调用工具和修改自身组件，安全自我改进面临关键问题：奖励模型或自动评审等门控能否可靠判断一项更新是否应被接受。本文将智能体建模为程序，把改进定义为可能不可计算的语言语义分数，形式化门控可计算性与真实语义改进之间的结构性错配。该分析揭示了自动自我改进门控的根本困难，为安全评估自我修改提供了理论框架。
papers.abstract_en: With the rise of large language models, agentic systems are becoming increasingly autonomous, as they write code, call tools, revise prompts, and propose modifications to their own components. This autonomy raises a fundamental question for safe self-improvement: can an automated gate like a reward model or an automated reviewer reliably decide whether a proposed update should be accepted? The difficulty is structural. The gate must be a terminating, computable procedure, while the property we ultimately care about, namely whether an update is a genuine semantic improvement, depends on potentially unbounded program behavior. We formalize this mismatch by modeling agents as programs and defining improvement in terms of a semantic score that need not be computable. We study two evaluation abstractions. The first is a certifier that approves or rejects an update. The second is a search procedure that, given access to a proposal generator, attempts to output some improving candidate if one exists. We show that, in the fully general setting, no terminating procedure can simultaneously guarantee reliability (never accepting a non-improvement) and non-conservatism (never missing an available improvement): self-referential constructions can force any such gate or searcher to fail. Randomized gates with bounded error face the same limit. We then identify a standard decidable regime used in practice (bounded evaluation and a finite proposal budget) under which exhaustive simulation yields a terminating search procedure with the desired guarantees. We also show the limit of this recovery: a chain of accepted updates can raise the bounded score in every round while the true score falls. Our results draw a boundary between unbounded, universal settings where correctness guarantees collapse and bounded settings where they can be recovered by design.

papers.title_en: Learning to Compose: Recursive Self-Improvement of Shared Executable Stacks for Zero-Shot Long-Horizon Robot Manipulation
papers.authors: Yangzhi Chen, Feiran Liu, Zishuo Wang, Zijian Jin, Xin Zhu, Lecheng Ruan, Wenjuan Han
papers.evidence: 面向机器人操作的共享可执行栈递归自我改进
papers.tldr: 该文指出单个机器人技能组合时常失败，如缺工具、完成信号失真或状态违反后继前提。作者提出Recursia递归自我改进框架，以共享可执行栈而非单个任务程序为改进单元，整合工具、技能契约、交接与验证器。方法利用执行轨迹归因失败并生成缺失工具或修复组件，配合泛化与回归门控筛选改进，提升了零样本长程操作表现。
papers.abstract_en: Individually competent robot skills can fail when composed: tools may lack a required capability, completion signals may misrepresent physical progress, and one skill may leave a state that violates its successor's prerequisites. We introduce Recursia, a recursive self-improvement framework that treats the shared executable stack, rather than individual task programs, as the persistent unit of improvement. The stack integrates tools, skills with execution contracts, handoffs, and verifiers. Source-side execution traces guide failure attribution and the generation of missing tools or repairs to existing shared components. Generality checks, mechanism tests, and paired selection and regression gates determine which changes become the next parent. The resulting stack is frozen and reused through declarative task adapters, allowing source-derived changes to support new compositions without target-side code repair. Experiments cover LIBERO-Pro Long simulation and a physical Franka FR3 equipped with a Franka Hand. In simulation, Recursia improves success over ASPIRE by 5.8 percentage points under Pos perturbations and 15.1 points under Task perturbations. Across three physical compositional target tasks, it improves mean success over the Skill Document Only baseline by 40 percentage points. Analyses of constituent execution, candidate rejection, and inference drivers distinguish local mechanism improvements from complete task success and characterize the cost of feedback-conditioned orchestration. These results examine shared executable interfaces as a concrete mechanism for compositional transfer in robot programming.

papers.authors: Xiaoyin Chen, Yizheng Huang, Yinglun Xu, Ziyun Zhao, Emmett McQuinn, Julie Liu, Hope Yao
papers.evidence: 自演化智能体重写自身框架以持续适应
papers.tldr: 该文关注部署中不断遇到新知识、工具与流程的LLM智能体，需持续适应又不遗忘旧任务。作者考察不改权重、仅通过重写提示、记忆与技能等框架来演化的非参数自演化智能体，在四个漂移任务流上评测三类代表性方法。结果显示这类智能体具备一定持续学习能力但存在局限，为自演化智能体的持续学习性质提供了实证分析。
papers.abstract_en: Large language model agents are often deployed in environments where new knowledge, tools, and workflows keep arriving. Such an agent is therefore expected to adapt continually, learning new tasks as they arrive without forgetting earlier ones. This resembles the continual learning problem, but at a pace that conventional gradient updates cannot sustain. Nonparametric self-evolving agents are a natural alternative: they adapt by rewriting their own harness, such as prompts, memory, and skills, from task feedback while the model weights stay frozen. We study whether such agents are effective continual learners across four drifting task streams that shift in topic, workflow, or domain (built from BIRD, BFCL, and ScienceWorld). Evaluating three representative methods spanning experience retrieval and self-modification (ReasoningBank, GEPA, and Meta-Harness), we find that although self-evolution improves aggregate performance on most streams, higher plasticity consistently comes at the cost of stability. Specifically, self-modifying methods apply global edits to a shared prompt or workspace, interfering with unseen tasks and overwriting earlier knowledge as the stream shifts. Conversely, similarity-based memory retrieval localizes updates across distant domains, but still retrieves foreign memories on unseen tasks and suffers from retrieval collision when similar queries require conflicting workflows. These findings show that current self-evolving agents remain incomplete continual learners.

papers.title_en: Learning What to Remember: Resource-Efficient Self-Improvement for Lifelong Agents
papers.authors: Guannan Lai, Zi-Yang Bai, Jun-Peng Jiang, Han-Jia Ye
papers.evidence: 联合约束下终身智能体的资源高效自我改进
papers.tldr: 自我改进智能体希望在部署后持续从经验中学习，但当生成、交互与记忆资源受限时，积累更多经验未必带来更好决策。作者发现在严格约束下多种终身记忆方法相比简单检索甚至无记忆智能体收益有限，进而研究智能体应如何判断哪些经验真正值得复用以改进未来决策，为资源高效的自我改进提供了新见解。
papers.abstract_en: Self-improving agents aim to continuously improve their behavior by learning from experience after deployment. However, accumulating and reusing more experience does not necessarily lead to better decisions, particularly when generation, interaction, and memory resources are jointly constrained. Under such stringent constraints, we find that several existing lifelong-memory methods provide limited benefits over simple retrieval or even no-memory agents. This reveals a fundamental challenge for resource-efficient self-improvement: agents must learn not only which past experiences are relevant, but which are actually worth reusing to improve future decisions. When memory capacity and opportunities for reasoning and recovery are limited, retrieving an ineffective experience can consume scarce resources and hinder downstream execution. To address this challenge, we propose TokenWorth, a lightweight feedback-driven memory adaptation framework that learns query-dependent memory worth from sparse execution feedback. Without updating the backbone model, TokenWorth uses the learned worth to guide both experience retrieval and bounded memory management, enabling the agent to continually adapt how it reuses accumulated experience. Across three LifelongAgentBench environments and both local and API-based deployments, TokenWorth achieves the highest task success rate while using the fewest output tokens among the evaluated methods under the specified resource budgets. These results suggest that effective self-improvement under resource constraints depends not on accumulating more experience, but on learning what is worth remembering. Our code is publicly available at https://github.com/AIGNLAI/TokenWorth.

papers.title_en: RSI Control: Can AI Models Perform Covert Sabotage in the Self-Improvement Process?
papers.evidence: 研究前沿模型自主训练后继模型时的安全风险
papers.tldr: 递归自我改进中前沿模型参与训练下一代模型已成现实，但该过程的安全性关注不足，被错位对齐的模型可能塑造后继模型的知识与行为。作者构建 RSI 控制竞技场，让前沿模型作为自主研发智能体在完成良性训练流水线任务的同时执行隐蔽侧任务，试图向后继模型植入错位属性。测试平台包含三类共十六项侧任务，用于评估控制手段能否发现并阻止此类隐蔽破坏。该工作把 AI 控制视角引入自我改进流程的安全评估。
papers.abstract_en: Recursive self-improvement, in which frontier AI models work on training the next generation, is quickly becoming a reality. However, the safety of this process has received far less attention than it should. A misaligned model training its successor can shape what that successor knows, how it behaves, and what it wants, and the harm carries forward into the next generation. We study this risk through the lens of AI control. We introduce RSI Control Arena, a testbed in which a frontier model, acting as an autonomous R\&D agent, is given a benign main task from a stage of a successor model's training pipeline together with a covert side task to install a misaligned property in the successor. The testbed contains 16 side tasks in three classes, forming 22 task pairs with main tasks that span the pipeline from data curation to reinforcement learning. We evaluate six frontier models as agents against LLM monitors that read the transcript of the run and the agent's reasoning. We observe that every model completes a substantial share of the side tasks without degrading the main-task performance, including side tasks that make the successor itself a better saboteur. Under minimal instructions to stay covert, models already produce successful attacks that monitors fail to detect, and providing a short list of evasion tactics further reduces the detection rate. Monitors with access to agent's reasoning detects most attacks, but not all. Our results indicate that recursive self-improvement raises significant safety concerns, and that strong safety effort should be in place before models are trusted with greater responsibility of training their successors.

papers.title_en: Toward Recursive Self-Improvement in Physical AI
papers.authors: Meng Luo, Zechen Bai, Shanqing Xu, Yanlin Li, Kaixin Li, Mengchen Qian, Weifeng Lu, Ran Zhang, Yingtian Zou, Ziyang Luo, Wei Chen, Hongzhan Lin
papers.evidence: 将递归自我改进置于机器人学习中并探讨改进过程本身的改进
papers.tldr: 递归自我改进指系统不仅改进行为，还改进其改进过程本身，数字智能体已通过重写自身代码并用可执行测试校验来验证这一点。作者将 RSI 置于机器人学习语境，梳理从提升机器人能力到提升生成这些能力的过程的路径。文章分析物理经验如何强化改进机制，以及何时这些增益能支撑机制自身的进一步自我改进。该立场论文为物理 AI 中的递归自我改进提供了研究路线图。
papers.abstract_en: Recursive self-improvement (RSI) describes a system that improves not only its behavior but also the process by which it improves. Recent digital agents test this idea by rewriting their own code and checking each version with executable tests. Bringing these mechanisms into the physical world requires learning from partial observations through costly trials, while accounting for changing operating conditions and potentially irreversible consequences. We position RSI within robot learning and trace pathways from improving robot capabilities to improving the processes that generate them. We examine how physical experience can strengthen these improvement mechanisms and when the resulting gains can support further self-improvement of the mechanisms themselves. Gains carry forward only when feedback addresses remaining learning needs, the receiving component can use the change, its value survives changes in tasks or hardware, and continued practice remains safe and affordable. Existing studies, concentrated in manipulation, support behavioral improvement, benefits to later learning, and procedure improvement. Some systems also change the improver's knowledge or tools, but the physical studies reviewed here have yet to isolate gains attributable to recursion. We synthesize these findings into evaluation principles and research directions for machines that, trial by trial, safely improve the way they improve.

papers.title_en: HarnessMM: Recursive Self-Improvement for Harness Token Efficiency
papers.authors: Yuhua Jiang, Chang Xu, Feifei Gao, Li Zhao
papers.evidence: 利用递归自我改进提升智能体框架的令牌效率与计算成本
papers.tldr: 智能体框架在工具反馈后常重复调用推理，即使先前调用已确定下一步动作，造成令牌浪费。作者提出HarnessMM，通过受保护决策复用和递归自我改进提升框架令牌效率。RSI根据训练反馈迭代精炼配套框架配置，并由验证选择部署配置；模型-工具边界控制器复用已解析决策替代后续推理回调，同时保持actor权重不变。可执行决策图保存动作、参数、因果依赖和公开守卫，该工作从效率角度评估并优化RSI机制。
papers.abstract_en: Agent harnesses repeatedly invoke reasoning after tool feedback, even when an earlier call has already fixed the next action. We introduce HarnessMM (Harness Minus Minus), a method for improving harness token efficiency through guarded decision reuse and recursive self-improvement (RSI). RSI iteratively refines companion harness configurations from training feedback, with validation selecting the configuration for deployment. A controller at the model-tool boundary reuses resolved decisions to replace later reasoning callbacks while actor weights remain fixed. Executable Decision Graphs store exact actions, literal arguments, causal dependencies, and public guards. Guarded Decision Reuse activates these persistent decisions from observed receipts; Certified Callback Substitution executes them through the native interface and records removal of the registered slow callback. New semantic decisions, unsupported evidence, and selector abstention invoke the original actor again. The representation restricts what feedback may change, while complete-task measurements establish quality and cost. On HumanEval, HarnessMM preserves Codex success at 90.82\% while reducing Tokens/task (k) from 66.72 to 47.02 (29.54\% saving). For DeepSeek Harness, success rises from 71.43\% to 85.71\% while Tokens/task (k) fall from 96.28 to 11.62 (87.93\% saving). A separate MBPP ablation measures 26.91\% lower cost than single-use graphs and 19.52\% lower cost than retained callbacks. These results establish guarded decision reuse as a practical way to reduce repeated reasoning in existing harnesses.

papers.title_en: Efficiency vs Capability in the Intelligence Explosion
papers.evidence: 对AI研究自动化中的能力边际与算力效率边际建模并校准，评估自我维持的加速
papers.tldr: 关于智能爆炸的讨论常把能力提升与效率提升混为一谈。作者构建AI研究的任务自动化模型，区分能力边际与效率边际，并用近期AI进展数据校准两者。结果显示能力进展可能足以支撑自我维持的加速，而效率进展处于临界状态。该工作为评估递归自我改进系统的算力成本、效率与加速条件提供了量化框架。
papers.abstract_en: AI progress can feed back into AI research in two ways. Capability improvements allow AIs to perform a larger share of AI research tasks, while efficiency improvements raise AI research output per unit of compute on tasks already automated. In a task automation model of AI research, I show that a software-driven intelligence explosion - a self-sustaining acceleration in AI progress with fixed compute and human labor - requires both margins to improve sufficiently fast, and neither margin can substitute for the other. To see whether these conditions hold, I calibrate both margins with data on recent AI progress. I estimate that capability progress is likely fast enough to support an SIE, while efficiency progress is on the knife-edge. In Monte Carlo simulations, an SIE occurs in 49% of draws, indicating that an SIE is plausible but uncertain based on historical trends in AI progress. The single largest source of uncertainty is the rate of efficiency progress, whose uncertainty is responsible for 45% of the uncertainty about whether an SIE occurs, more than all other parameters combined. Thus, better data on efficiency progress in frontier models is essential for understanding the likelihood of an SIE.
